_comment: PIPELINES ARE SEEDED NOW, AND THEY DELIBERATELY WERE NOT BEFORE.
The root .mj-sync.json used to say pipelines are per-deployment data rather than vocabulary, and
that was the right call while installing the app and configuring it were the same act. The dev->test
process changed the premise: 'install the app and test it' is now the workflow, and an app that
installs with no pipeline is an app where nobody can create a deal or render a board column. A
default nobody wants is cheaper to change than a blocker nobody expected.
THE COMPANY IS THE AWKWARD PART, and the reason this was deferred. Pipeline.CompanyID is NOT NULL
and stays that way (docs/DECISIONS.md D5), so a seeded pipeline has to name a selling company --
and companies are MJ core data that belong to the deployment, not to this app. The lookup below
resolves 'Default Company' with ?create -- the explicit auto-create form, because the root config's
autoCreateMissingRecords does NOT cover a failed @lookup — measured: the push halts on it. It is
the only option that leaves the app usable on a bare install. A deployment with a real company
should repoint these two rows or rename that one; scripts/seed-demo-data.sh does exactly that for

This is the ONLY place sales' metadata reaches into MJ core data. It is worth knowing that, which
is why it is written here rather than assumed.
